problems.title: A positive double-angle cosine
problems.question: For 0<α<π/4, sinα+cosα=1.1. Find cos2α.
problems.idea: Square the given sum to find sin2α.
steps: cos²2α=1−0.0441=0.9559. Since 2α is acute, take the positive root.

problems.title: A range after cancelling a tangent identity
problems.question: Find the range of f(x)=cos2x·2tan x/(1−tan²x).
problems.idea: Simplify, but retain all forbidden inputs.
steps: The original expression excludes cos x=0 and tan²x=1.
The extrema sin2x=±1 occur exactly at tan²x=1 and are therefore excluded.
Every value strictly between −1 and 1 is attained at an allowed input; zero is attained at x=0.

problems.title: A two-angle numerator factors
problems.question: Simplify [2cos²αcos²β+2sin²αsin²β−1]/(cos2αcos2β), assuming its denominator is nonzero.
problems.idea: Rewrite each square with double angles.
steps: After subtracting 1, the numerator equals the denominator.

problems.title: A square placed on the faces of a dihedral angle
problems.question: A square’s vertices lie on different faces of a 40° dihedral angle. Which listed angle can occur between a square side and the dihedral edge?
problems.idea: Two vertices on each face form opposite square sides parallel to the dihedral edge.
formulas: If a plane cuts two intersecting planes in parallel lines, those lines are parallel to their intersection.
steps: Those two square sides run parallel to the dihedral edge; the other two are perpendicular to them.
Thus a square side can make 90° with the dihedral edge, as listed.
A construction uses two equal parallel segments on the faces, parallel to the edge, choosing their separation equal to their length.

problems.title: Count regular pyramids with integer edge lengths
problems.question: Count regular pyramids with positive integer edge lengths, at most 12 edges, and total edge length 20.
problems.idea: An n-gonal regular pyramid has n base edges a and n lateral edges l.
steps: n∈{3,4,5,6} and n divides 20, so n=4 or 5.
For n=4, a+l=5. The valid pairs (a,l) are (1,4),(2,3). The others violate l>a/√2.
For n=5, a+l=4. The valid pairs are (1,3),(2,2); (3,1) is too short laterally.
There are 2+2 possibilities.

problems.title: A cosine of two inverse-trig angles
problems.question: Evaluate $\cos(\arcsin(1/3)+\arccos(2/3))$.
problems.idea: Both principal angles are acute.
formulas: cos(u+v)=cos u cos v−sin u sin v.
steps: For u=arcsin(1/3), sin u=1/3, cos u=2√2/3.
For v=arccos(2/3), cos v=2/3, sin v=√5/3.
Substitute to obtain (4√2−√5)/9.

problems.title: The root closest to zero on the negative side
problems.question: Find the greatest negative solution of 1+cos x+cos2x+cos3x=0.
problems.idea: Factor the cosine sum.
steps: The sum is 2cos x(cos x+cos2x)=4cos x cos(3x/2)cos(x/2).
The negative zero nearest 0 comes from cos(3x/2)=0 at x=−π/3.
The nearest negative zeros from the other factors are −π/2 and −π.

problems.title: A telescoping trigonometric sum
problems.question: Find the maximum of sin7x−2(cos2x+cos4x+cos6x)sin x.
problems.idea: Expand each cosine product into a difference of sines.
steps: Summing k=1,2,3 makes the middle terms cancel, giving sin7x−sin x.
The whole function is therefore sin x, whose maximum is 1.

problems.title: A lateral edge of a square frustum
problems.question: In a regular square-pyramid frustum, the total length of lateral edges equals the difference of base perimeters. Find the inclination of a lateral edge to the base.
problems.idea: Let square base edges be B>b and lateral edge l.
formulas: 4l=4(B−b); horizontal projection of a lateral edge=(B−b)/√2.
steps: Thus l=B−b and cos(inclination)=1/√2.

problems.title: Compare two apex angles of a square pyramid
problems.question: Adjacent face apothems of a regular square pyramid make angle α; a lateral face’s apex angle is β. Which listed relation is possible?
problems.idea: Compute the two cosines in terms of height h and base half-edge t.
steps: The first denominator is smaller, so cosα>cosβ.
Both angles lie between 0° and 90°, where cosine decreases. Therefore α<β.

problems.title: An odd-power sine sequence
problems.question: The sequence is sin x,sin³x,sin⁵x,sin⁷x,… . Which of the listed behaviours is impossible?
problems.idea: Set s=sin x; consecutive terms have ratio s²≥0.
formulas: Terms are s(s²)ⁿ for n=0,1,2,…; all are in [−1,1].
steps: Every nonzero term has the same sign, so a sign-alternating sequence is impossible.
A strictly decreasing arithmetic progression is also impossible because it would be unbounded below.
A decreasing geometric sequence is possible for 0<s<1. Constant and arithmetic cases occur at s=0 or ±1.
problems.answer: Both “sign-alternating” and “decreasing arithmetic progression” are impossible.
problems.note: The source uses powers sin³x,sin⁵x, not sin3x,sin5x. With the printed powers there are two impossible listed behaviours.

problems.title: Count sine roots on an open interval
problems.question: How many roots of sin5x=1/2 lie in (0,π/2)?
problems.idea: Count standard sine angles in the expanded interval.
steps: The allowed t values are π/6,5π/6,13π/6.
The next,17π/6, is outside the interval.

problems.title: Half of all digit sums are even
problems.question: How many six-digit numbers have an even digit sum?
problems.idea: After fixing the first five digits, exactly five last digits give the required parity.
formulas: First digit:9 choices; next four:10⁴ choices; final digit:5 choices.
steps: The total is 9·10⁴·5=450000.

problems.title: Lateral area from a dihedral angle and a section
problems.question: A regular square pyramid has interior dihedral angle 120° at a lateral edge. Its diagonal-section area is 40. Find lateral area.
problems.idea: The dihedral condition makes height equal to base half-edge.
formulas: Let half-edge t and height h. cos60°=t²/(t²+h²), so h=t.
steps: The face apothem is t√2. Diagonal-section area=(1/2)(2t√2)t=t²√2=40.
Lateral area=4·[(1/2)(2t)(t√2)]=4t²√2.

problems.title: Equal lateral edges above an isosceles triangle
problems.question: A pyramid’s base is an isosceles triangle with base 6 and altitude 9. All lateral edges are 13. Find the pyramid height.
problems.idea: The apex projects to the base circumcentre.
steps: The height is √(13²−5²)=√144.

problems.title: Seven children choose different problems
problems.question: Seven children each solve one of 10 problems. Find the probability they all solve different problems.
problems.idea: Under independent uniform choices, count injective assignments.
problems.note: This assumes each child chooses independently and uniformly. None of the printed choices matches the resulting probability.

problems.title: A positive number cannot be a root here
problems.question: Choose integers b,c independently from 1,…,10 in x²+bx+c=0. What is the probability that c is a root?
problems.idea: Substitute the proposed positive root.
steps: Every factor is positive, so the value cannot be zero for any permitted b,c.

problems.title: Sum absolute binomial coefficients
problems.question: Find the sum of the absolute values of all coefficients in (2x−3y)¹⁰.
problems.idea: After taking absolute values, the coefficients are those of (2x+3y)¹⁰.
formulas: Set x=y=1 in the positive-coefficient expansion.
steps: The sum is (2+3)¹⁰.

problems.title: A short space diagonal of a regular hexagonal prism
problems.question: Every edge of a regular hexagonal prism is 4. Find a short space diagonal.
problems.idea: Its base projection is a short hexagon diagonal.
steps: The diagonal is 2a=8.

problems.title: Lateral area above a tangential trapezoid
problems.question: A right prism has a tangential trapezoid base of midline 12 and height 3. Find lateral area.
problems.idea: Tangency makes the leg sum equal the base sum.
steps: Multiply 48 by 3.

problems.title: Recognize a complete binomial expansion
problems.question: Evaluate the printed sum of the six fifth-degree binomial terms in 2x−3 and 5−2x.
problems.idea: The coefficients 1,5,10,10,5,1 are the fifth row of Pascal’s triangle.
steps: Set u=2x−3,v=5−2x. Then u+v=2.
The sum is 2⁵.

problems.title: A linear form on an absolute-value diamond
problems.question: Maximize 3x−2y subject to |x|+|y|≤1.
problems.idea: Bound each signed term by its absolute value.
steps: Thus the value is at most 3.
At x=1,y=0 the constraint holds and the value is 3.

problems.title: The shortest hypotenuse for a fixed inradius
problems.question: A right triangle has inradius 3(√2−1). Find its least possible hypotenuse.
problems.idea: The sum of the legs is at most √2 times the hypotenuse.
steps: Equality holds when the legs are equal, giving an isosceles right triangle.

problems.title: Parallel parameter vectors with an exceptional case
problems.question: Find m such that (m,m+1,m+2) and (3−m,4,2m+4) are parallel.
problems.idea: Use the third components when they are nonzero, then check the exceptional value.
formulas: If m≠−2, the proportionality factor must be 2.
steps: Then 3−m=2m gives m=1, and the second components also agree: 4=2(1+1).
If m=−2, the vectors are (−2,−1,0),(5,4,0), which are not proportional.

problems.title: No perpendicular vertex-radius pairs in a cube
problems.question: O is the cube centre. How many pairs among its eight vertex position vectors have dot product zero?
problems.idea: Use coordinates centred at O.
formulas: Up to a common scale, every vertex vector is (±1,±1,±1).
steps: A dot product is a sum of three numbers, each +1 or −1.
An odd number of such terms cannot sum to zero.
